digest:
Recent work continues to deepen the holographic dictionary, sharpening our understanding of bulk–boundary dynamics in AdS$_3$ and beyond.  The Maxwell–Chern–Simons–Matter paper delivers an exact photon propagator at large $N$, revealing a split spin‑one boundary spectrum governed by the Chern–Simons level and mapping out phase diagrams for scalar and fermionic matter.  In a complementary direction, the Spectral Edge study introduces a modular bootstrap that incorporates L‑functions, yielding a refined bound on the lightest primary gap that remains within $O(1)$ of the BTZ threshold for almost all large‑$c$ theories.  Quantum gravity on the bulk cone shows that null‑geodesic singularities are smoothed out in the dual CFT, while the Quasinormal Modes paper demonstrates that regular AdS black holes replace real null‑geodesic singularities with smooth bumps associated with complex null geodesics, offering a holographic signature of interior regularization.

On the amplitude side, the Inverse KLT kernel work builds a topological and combinatorial framework for Kawai–Lewellen–Tye relations in AdS string amplitudes, employing twisted de Rham theory, associahedral chambers, and Drinfeld associators to construct an intersection matrix that serves as the inverse KLT kernel and its field‑theory limit.  This dovetails with the Plabic promotions paper, which extends plabic tangles to quantum cluster quasi‑homomorphisms preserving the dual canonical basis, providing new tools for higher‑point scattering and cluster algebra structures.  Defect CFT dynamics receive fresh insight from the Holographic surface defect RG flows paper, which constructs non‑supersymmetric surface defects in $mathcal{N}=4$ SYM, verifies the $b$‑theorem, and elucidates defect RG flows at strong coupling.  Finally, the 3D de Sitter from complex Virasoro TQFT paper delivers exact partition functions on spherical cone manifolds via analytic continuation of Virasoro TQFT amplitudes, linking knot invariants to static‑patch correlators and extending the construction to knotted worldlines and Seifert manifolds.  Together, these results underscore a vibrant interplay between holography, integrable structures, and higher‑point amplitude techniques that will shape future research in the field.

papers.title: Twisted scattering from Chern-Simons theory
papers.authors: Guillermo Arias-Tamargo, Philip Boyle Smith, Rishi Mouland, Max Vel\'asquez Cotini Hutt
papers.abstract: We consider boundary conditions of two-dimensional Dirac fermions which preserve a non-anomalous continuous symmetry which acts differently on the left- and right-movers. Such boundaries are equivalent to topological defects of Weyl fermions preserving the symmetry. We give a general construction of such defects for conformally-embedded symmetries using Chern-Simons theory. They always exist and can be realised as half-space gauging defects for some finite categorical symmetry. Using this technology, we compute the twist lines to which fermions become attached upon scattering through the defect, the boundary central charge of the corresponding folded boundary state, and its mod-2 valued SPT class. As applications, we first consider abelian symmetries and find agreement with known results in the literature. We then study a novel example where an $SU(2) \times SU(4) \times U(1)^2$ symmetry is preserved. In contrast to the abelian case, the twist lines are intrinsically non-invertible and belong to either a $\text{TY}(\mathbb{Z}_3 \times \mathbb{Z}_3)$ or $\text{Rep}(\mathbb{S}_3) \times \mathbb{Z}_3$ symmetry depending on whether scattering is to the left or the right.
papers.summary: This paper constructs boundary conditions for 2D Dirac fermions that preserve a continuous symmetry acting differently on left- and right-movers, interpreting them as topological defects in Chern‑Simons theory. It computes twist lines, boundary central charges, and SPT classes, and applies the framework to both abelian and a novel non‑abelian SU(2)×SU(4)×U(1)^2 example with non‑invertible twist lines.

papers.title: Finding CFTs from spatial positivity of partition functions
papers.authors: L\'eo Buisine, Horacio Casini, Leandro Martinek
papers.abstract: We discuss a positivity property for partition functions that generalizes modular invariance and which is here conjectured to hold for general 2D CFTs. We show its relation to positivity properties of R\'enyi entropies and its meaning in terms of topological defect lines. We apply the conjecture to find consistent local unitary CFT models which are not necessarily modular invariant.
papers.summary: The paper proposes a new positivity condition for 2D CFT partition functions that extends modular invariance, linking it to R'enyi entropy positivity and topological defect lines. Using this conjecture, the authors construct consistent local unitary CFTs that need not be modular invariant, offering a novel way to explore non‑standard CFT spectra.

papers.title: Collinear Gluons from Gravity: Poincar\'e-Birkhoff-Witt Decomposition and Twisted Intersections
papers.authors: Jin Dong, Stephan Stieberger
papers.abstract: We give an explicit reconstruction of subleading collinear Yang--Mills amplitudes from one-graviton amplitudes in Einstein--Yang--Mills theory and its string corrections. We realize the monodromy kernel in the mixed open-closed string relation as a weighted Lie-algebraic recursion on words of gluon labels. At order $\alpha'^r$, its output contains at most $r$ Lie factors. The Poincar\'e--Birkhoff--Witt (PBW) theorem decomposes the space spanned by gluon orderings into sectors whose dimensions are given by unsigned Stirling numbers of the first kind. Appropriate shuffle sums of one-graviton amplitudes extract the degree-$r$ sector, for which the string-period matrix drops out. Accordingly, we show that the reconstruction coefficients factor into linear kinematic factors over the product of bipartition factors. Finally, we express the reconstruction coefficients as twisted intersection numbers between Parke--Taylor forms and explicit forest cocycles constructed recursively from logarithmic four-point differentials.
papers.summary: This paper presents a systematic method to reconstruct subleading collinear Yang–Mills amplitudes from one‑graviton amplitudes in Einstein–Yang–Mills theory, interpreting the monodromy kernel as a weighted Lie‑algebraic recursion on gluon words. It further shows that the PBW decomposition isolates a degree‑r sector where the string‑period matrix drops out, enabling the reconstruction coefficients to be expressed as twisted intersection numbers between Parke–Taylor forms and recursively defined forest cocycles.

papers.title: Reentrant $d=2+1$ Superfluidity at High Temperature
papers.authors: Subham Dutta Chowdhury, Joan Elias Miro
papers.abstract: We present a UV-complete model with a global $U(1)$ symmetry in $d=2+1$ dimensions that exhibits a Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) ordered phase at arbitrarily high temperatures. A careful separation of scales yields a two-dimensional Euclidean effective field theory whose construction remains perturbatively controlled even when its soft modes become strongly coupled. We determine the BKT phase boundary by carefully matching this theory to existing lattice Monte Carlo results. The high-temperature phase supports gapless static modes and algebraically decaying correlations even as $T\to\infty$.
papers.summary: The paper constructs a UV‑complete 2+1 dimensional U(1) model that exhibits a Berezinskii‑Kosterlitz‑Thouless phase at arbitrarily high temperatures, deriving the phase boundary by matching a perturbatively controlled 2D effective theory to lattice Monte‑Carlo data. It shows that even in the high‑temperature limit the system retains gapless static modes and algebraic correlations, revealing a novel reentrant superfluid behavior.

papers.title: Defect flows from functional relations in the asymptotic semiring
papers.authors: Federico Ambrosino, Anatoly Konechny, Ingo Runkel, G\'erard M. T. Watts
papers.abstract: We study perturbations of topological defects by a relevant holomorphic defect field in two-dimensional conformal field theory. This produces translation invariant defects and these necessarily flow to topological defects in the infrared. Translation invariant defects form a monoidal category which extends the fusion category of topological defects. We argue that the renormalisation group flow defines a semiring homomorphism from the semiring of translation invariant defects to an "asymptotic semiring" which we construct from topological defects. The semiring homomorphism preserves functional relations, and we illustrate in the example of Virasoro minimal models that the resulting relations in the asymptotic semiring constrain the defect flow endpoints. The companion paper [1] contains a detailed study of such defect flows in several minimal models, both numerically and analytically.
papers.summary: The paper investigates how perturbing topological defects with a relevant holomorphic defect field in 2D CFT generates translation‑invariant defects that flow to topological ones in the IR, and shows that the RG flow induces a semiring homomorphism preserving functional relations. In Virasoro minimal models, these relations constrain the possible defect flow endpoints, offering a new algebraic perspective on defect dynamics.

papers.title: From bulk flows to boundary generators and costs
papers.authors: Rafael Carrasco, Carlos P\'erez-Pardavila
papers.abstract: Holographic complexity admits a broad family of bulk observables, yet their relation to boundary state-preparation costs remains unclear. We propose a local prescription that associates suitable bulk observables with quadratic cost geometries on families of states prepared by Euclidean sources. Building on the holographic transport of bulk Hamiltonian flows to Euclidean preparation sources, we use the Hessian of the transported generator at a stationary reference state to define a candidate cost metric. When this Hessian is positive definite, the minimised preparation energy reproduces the change in the bulk observable to quadratic order. We characterise the resulting preparation penalties relative to the Fubini-Study metric and compute them for the maximal volume in scalar perturbations of AdS$_3$. At large-conformal dimension, we recover the known proportionality between cost and Fubini-Study metrics. At finite dimension, we obtain positive but generally unequal penalties for source variations that displace the bulk field and its conjugate momentum, breaking this proportionality even for a single scalar operator. We further study a deformation of volume by quadratic scalar and gradient terms in the large-dimension regime, determining how the couplings modify the penalties and constrain positivity. These additions selectively change field-displacement costs, with the gradient term introducing mode dependence. Our results provide an explicit local connection between the choice of bulk observables and the assignment of boundary preparation penalties.
papers.summary: The paper proposes a local prescription linking bulk observables to quadratic cost geometries for Euclidean state preparation, using the Hessian of transported generators to define a cost metric that reproduces bulk observable changes to quadratic order. It then applies this framework to scalar perturbations of AdS$_3$, computing preparation penalties relative to the Fubini-Study metric and exploring how additional scalar and gradient terms affect these penalties, thereby establishing a concrete connection between bulk observable choices and boundary preparation costs.

papers.title: 3D de Sitter from complex Virasoro TQFT: Observers and knots
papers.authors: Jeevan Chandra, Diego Liska, Boris Post
papers.abstract: The Euclidean saddles of 3D Einstein gravity with positive cosmological constant are spherical three-manifolds. When one adds a heavy observer, the backreacted saddles are spherical cone manifolds, with a conical singularity along the observer worldline. We propose exact gravitational partition functions at fixed topology on a class of spherical cone manifolds that undergo hyperbolic-to-spherical transitions as the cone angles increase. Our construction relies on a careful analytic continuation of the product of two Virasoro TQFT partition functions. We test the proposal by showing that the exact partition functions exponentiate in the semiclassical limit to the spherical volume, in agreement with the gravitational on-shell action. This leads to a spherical volume conjecture for the product of continued Virasoro TQFT amplitudes. As further evidence, we relate the theta and tetrahedron graph amplitudes to the two-point function and out-of-time-ordered four-point function of operators on a massive observer's worldline. In appropriate limits, we recover the static patch scalar two-point function with finite observer backreaction and the semiclassical effects of observer recoil. In addition, we analyze examples with knotted worldlines and reproduce their spherical volumes. We also apply our prescription to Seifert manifolds, which are off-shell in AdS$_3$ gravity but admit dS$_3$ saddles, and find agreement with their spherical volumes semiclassically. Finally, using Dehn surgery on torus knots and links, we obtain partition functions on smooth spherical three-manifolds.
papers.summary: The authors construct exact partition functions for 3D de Sitter gravity on spherical cone manifolds by analytically continuing products of Virasoro TQFT amplitudes, showing that these exponentiate to the spherical volume and match semiclassical on‑shell actions. They further relate graph amplitudes to two‑ and four‑point functions on massive observer worldlines, recover static‑patch correlators with backreaction, and extend the construction to knotted worldlines, Seifert manifolds, and smooth spherical three‑manifolds via Dehn surgery.

papers.title: Big Crunching Your Big Bang: Doubly Warped Time-Dependent Type II Flux Backgrounds and Scale Separation
papers.authors: Kazi Fahim Reza Arko, Walid Hasan, M. Fahim Hoque, Ahmed Rakin Kamal
papers.abstract: We construct three analytic, doubly warped cosmological solutions of massless type IIA supergravity with different choices of fluxes, namely, $H_3$, $\tilde F_2$ and $\tilde F_4$ along internal directions. The $H_3$ solution also belongs to the common NS--NS sector of type IIB. Our solutions show that, without localised sources, nonconstant warping on a smooth compact space is possible. We derive their eleven-dimensional uplifts and four-dimensional Einstein-frame cosmology. Each universe undergoes (decelerating) expansion from a Big Bang, reaches a maximum size, and undergoes contraction towards a Big Crunch. We also analyse the scale separation of these backgrounds and find that they exhibit a small Einstein frame Hubble scale to KK mass ratio $\frac{|H_E|}{m_{\mathrm{KK}}}\ll1,$ although for a brief period of time, around the maxima of the scale factor in the Einstein frame. Finally, we analyse the supersymmetry of these backgrounds, which demonstrates that all three solutions break all forms of type IIA supersymmetry.
papers.summary: The authors present three analytic, doubly warped cosmological solutions in massless type IIA supergravity, each featuring distinct fluxes and exhibiting a Big Bang–Big Crunch evolution with a brief period of scale separation. The solutions lack localized sources and supersymmetry, and are uplifted to eleven dimensions, but do not directly address holographic or conformal field theory concepts.

papers.title: Pressure in Wilsonian effective field theory
papers.authors: Vin\'icius Bernardes, Atakan Hilmi F{\i}rat
papers.abstract: We study the exponential rolling tachyon solution in Wilsonian effective field theory as a model for rolling tachyons in open string field theory. Although this solution exhibits runaway oscillations towards the future similar to its counterparts in string field theory, its pressure is shown to be consistent with the underlying bare theory, but only up to a finite time. The rest of the evolution of the pressure is instead governed by a solution that is oscillatory towards the past and regular at late times. We conjecture that the late time physics of rolling tachyons in open string field theory may be captured by the solutions that are different from the standard rolling tachyon solutions based on this analysis.
papers.summary: This paper investigates the exponential rolling tachyon solution within a Wilsonian effective field theory framework, showing that its pressure matches the bare theory only up to a finite time before transitioning to a different oscillatory regime. The authors suggest that late-time dynamics of rolling tachyons in open string field theory may be captured by these alternative solutions.

papers.title: Fluids on null hypersurfaces and Carrollian hydrodynamics
papers.authors: Emil Have
papers.abstract: We study intrinsic ideal fluids on null hypersurfaces and their realisations by causal fluids living in the ambient spacetime. An embedded null hypersurface is equipped with an induced Carrollian structure with a temporal Weyl symmetry inherited from rescalings of the null generator, and we develop the corresponding null submanifold and variational calculus. The intrinsic fluid phases are classified according to their realisation of Carroll boosts and temporal Weyl symmetry. If we demand that an ambient fluid be confined to a null hypersurface, the ambient fluid velocity must be null, which realises an intrinsic zero-temperature Carrollian phase with unbroken Carroll boosts. In general, timelike or null ambient fluids will cross a null hypersurface and lead to an open Carrollian system. On a null foliation, the sources correspond to transport between null leaves. We then show that there exists a decoupling limit of a timelike ambient fluid which gives rise to an autonomous Carrollian fluid with spontaneously broken Carroll boosts and no source terms. This decoupling limit corresponds to an infinite boost while keeping the enthalpy finite and nonzero, which leads to a divergent ambient energy-momentum tensor. Nevertheless, the induced Carrollian responses do not see the divergent term and remain finite, and an independent Carroll boost Goldstone emerges from a subleading component of the ambient fluid velocity in this limit.
papers.summary: The paper develops a variational framework for ideal fluids living on null hypersurfaces, revealing how Carrollian symmetries and temporal Weyl invariance govern their dynamics and how a decoupling limit yields an autonomous Carrollian fluid with broken boosts. It connects ambient timelike or null fluids to intrinsic Carrollian phases, highlighting the role of null hypersurfaces in holographic fluid/gravity dualities and potential applications to null infinity physics.

papers.title: Maxwell-Chern-Simons-Matter in AdS$_3$
papers.authors: Dean Carmi, Riccardo Ciccone
papers.abstract: We study Maxwell-Chern-Simons theory on AdS$_3$ coupled to $N$ complex scalars or Dirac fermions, including sextic and Gross-Neveu interactions, respectively. First, we derive the bulk Maxwell-Chern-Simons propagator, clarifying how Dirichlet boundary conditions fix the contributions of the massive and flat sectors. Upon coupling to the matter sector, we work at large $N$ with $\kappa=k/N$ and $\alpha=Ne^2$ fixed, where $k$ is the Chern-Simons level. We determine the corresponding phase diagrams, and we resum matter insertions to obtain the photon propagator at leading order in large $N$, exactly in $\alpha$ and $\kappa$. Its poles determine the spin-one boundary spectrum, split into two helicity sectors by the Chern-Simons interaction. With Dirichlet boundary conditions, the unHiggsed scalar phase contains a protected chiral current, which is lifted by Higgsing. In the fermionic phases, the current persists for nonzero effective Chern-Simons level, with helicity determined by the induced level shift. At bulk conformal points, we extract large-$N$ BCFT data for the critical and tricritical scalar theories, as well as for the regular fermion and Gross-Neveu theories.
papers.summary: The paper constructs the bulk Maxwell–Chern–Simons propagator in AdS$_3$ and, at large $N$, resums matter loops to obtain the exact photon propagator, revealing a split spin‑one boundary spectrum governed by the Chern–Simons level. It maps out the phase diagram for scalar and fermionic matter, identifies protected chiral currents, and extracts large‑$N$ BCFT data for critical and tricritical scalar and fermion theories.

papers.title: A tale of three points: mixed and tensor bispectra beyond leading order in Horndeski gravity
papers.authors: Y. A. Ageeva, M. A. Stepanov
papers.abstract: We derive the primordial $\langle\zeta\zeta h\rangle$, $\langle\zeta hh\rangle$, and $\langle hhh\rangle$ bispectra in general Horndeski theory through first order in slow variation, retaining their complete momentum and helicity dependence. The calculation includes the time evolution of the cubic coefficients, the correction to the scale factor, the first-order scalar and tensor mode functions, and the corrected power-spectrum normalization. We verify the tensor-soft and scalar-soft Maldacena consistency relations at the same order. We also study finite squeezing and show that, when $c_S\neq c_T$, the relevant soft variable is the ratio $c_Tq/(c_Sk)$, leading to an acoustic crossover not captured by geometric squeezing alone. We construct the corresponding nonlinearity parameters and apply the general results to a nonsingular contracting model, in which the mixed bispectra retain sensitivity to the contraction parameter through the scalar propagation speed.
papers.summary: This paper computes the mixed and tensor bispectra in general Horndeski gravity to first order in slow variation, including full momentum and helicity dependence, and verifies Maldacena consistency relations. It also explores finite squeezing effects and applies the results to a nonsingular contracting model, highlighting sensitivity to the scalar propagation speed.

papers.title: Data analysis of millions of Type IIB flux vacua
papers.authors: Yuta Hamada, Yuma Uematsu, Masahito Yamazaki
papers.abstract: We study the vacuum structure of flux compactifications of type IIB string theory on the degree 18 hypersurface in $\mathbb{CP}^4_{1,1,1,6,9}$ with two effective complex structure moduli. We scan $30{,}770{,}178$ flux choices compatible with the tadpole bound, and use a gradient-based constrained minimization based on the SLSQP algorithm to identify candidates for local minima of the scalar potential, yielding a dataset of millions of candidate flux vacua. Using the $1{,}296{,}633$ reliable solutions selected from this dataset, we analyze distributions and correlations of various physical quantities such as vacuum expectation values of moduli and vacuum energy. Using quadratic flux invariants as input features, we train a classifier to identify solutions satisfying the numerical SUSY criterion $|V|<10^{-4.5}$. On a randomly selected test set, selecting the top-ranked $5\%$ recovers $47.2\%$ of the SUSY test solutions. We also use supervised regression to predict the potential and moduli field values. In the regression comparison, quadratic flux invariant inputs improve prediction of potential value and the complex-structure coordinates, while the vanilla six flux parameters give better predictions for the axio-dilaton coordinates under the tested settings.
papers.summary: This paper surveys millions of flux vacua in a specific type IIB compactification, using gradient-based minimization to find local minima and machine learning to classify supersymmetric solutions. It analyzes statistical distributions of moduli vevs and vacuum energies, and demonstrates that quadratic flux invariants improve regression predictions for potential and complex-structure moduli.

papers.title: Quantum field theory and four-manifolds: Perspectives from physics and geometry
papers.authors: Niklas Garner, Martijn Kool, Jan Manschot, Yuuji Tanaka
papers.abstract: These lecture notes are based on lecture series by the authors for the Summer School 2025 on ``Physical mathematics of quantum field theory" at the University of Massachusetts Amherst organized by Owen Gwilliam, Chris Elliott, and Matteo Lotito. The lectures centred around algebraic structures arising from twists of supersymmetric quantum field theories, correlation functions of topologically twisted supersymmetric gauge theories, and their mathematical counterparts as intersection-theoretic invariants associated to moduli spaces of instantons, semistable sheaves, or Higgs sheaves on four-manifolds or complex projective surfaces.
papers.summary: These notes review how twisting supersymmetric gauge theories yields topological field theories whose correlation functions compute intersection‑theoretic invariants of moduli spaces of instantons, sheaves, or Higgs bundles on four‑manifolds. They also discuss algebraic structures such as vertex algebras and factorization algebras that encode these invariants, offering a bridge between physical observables and geometric invariants.

papers.title: Amplified EFT corrections near exceptional QNMs
papers.authors: William L. Boyce, Jorge E. Santos
papers.abstract: We show that the ordinary expansion of EFT corrections to individual QNM frequencies breaks down at an exceptional QNM, and that these corrections become enhanced for near-exceptional QNMs. We give a brief argument for why this should generally happen, before numerically demonstrating this behaviour by calculating the $\alpha'^3$ corrections to QNMs of equal-spin Myers--Perry-AdS$_5$ black holes. This calculation corresponds to $\lambda^{-3/2}$ corrections to the poles of the retarded Green's function in the boundary CFT, where $\lambda$ is the 't Hooft coupling. Treating the coalescing pair together, we calculate the leading $\lambda^{-3/4}$ splitting at the uncorrected exceptional point and the $\lambda^{-3/2}$ displacement of the exceptional point in temperature and angular velocity. The background derivative expansion can remain valid while the nondegenerate expansion of individual frequencies fails. We discuss the implications for the full response and for other areas of black hole physics.
papers.summary: The authors demonstrate that effective field theory corrections to quasinormal mode frequencies diverge near exceptional QNMs, leading to enhanced $lambda^{-3/4}$ splittings and $lambda^{-3/2}$ shifts in the dual CFT poles. This analysis, performed for equal‑spin Myers–Perry–AdS$_5$ black holes, has implications for the validity of the derivative expansion and the structure of holographic response functions.

papers.title: The Stringy Photon Sphere
papers.authors: Ahmed Sheta
papers.abstract: The S matrix on an asymptotically-flat Schwarzschild black hole is studied as a function of position on $\mathcal{I}$. We derive the lightcone singularities that arise in the S matrix whenever the two points on $\mathcal{I}$ are connected by a bulk null geodesic. This includes geodesics orbiting near the photon sphere for a long time, whose kinematics determine the associated lightcone singularities. By turning on a finite string length $\ell_s$, worldsheet corrections are shown to shift the lightcone singularities into the complex time plane, resolving the singularities at real times. In particular, we derive the leading stringy resolution of the photon sphere singularities. We also compute stringy corrections to the eikonal quasinormal mode spectrum of Schwarzschild, and discuss the kinematics of strings orbiting the photon sphere.
papers.summary: The authors analyze the S‑matrix for scattering off a Schwarzschild black hole, identifying light‑cone singularities that arise whenever two points on future null infinity are linked by a bulk null geodesic, including those that linger near the photon sphere. By incorporating finite string length corrections, they show that these singularities are shifted into the complex time plane, yielding a stringy resolution of the photon‑sphere singularities and a modified eikonal quasinormal‑mode spectrum.

papers.title: Normal Matrix Model and Hyperelliptic Curves
papers.authors: Valdemar Melin
papers.abstract: We present a two-matrix model with a normal matrix with eigenvalues confined to contours in the upper half plane coupled to a Hermitian matrix. This generalizes the matrix model proposed by Jens Hoppe which corresponds to a single horizontal line. We solve the saddle point equations for several lines and show that the large-N free energy can be expressed in terms of hyperelliptic integrals. We show that the model describes a Coulomb gas in the presence of an infinite conducting boundary.
papers.summary: The paper extends a two-matrix normal model, solving saddle point equations for multiple contour configurations and expressing the large‑N free energy via hyperelliptic integrals. It interprets the system as a Coulomb gas near an infinite conducting boundary, offering a new solvable example of matrix models with complex eigenvalue support.

papers.title: Higher-Loop Vacuum Integrals on $S^D$
papers.authors: Varun Lochab, Frederik Denef
papers.abstract: We develop a new framework for evaluating higher-loop integrals for scalar fields on $S^D$. Starting from a Schwinger-parametric form for general higher-loop integrals on the sphere, it combines total-derivative identities with edge-contraction relations into a coupled linear system. To illustrate our method, we solve for all vacuum graphs through two loops. This includes, in particular, the two-loop three-melon, for which we construct the analytic solution for general $D$ and obtain explicit dimensionally regularized results at all integer dimensions.
papers.summary: The authors present a systematic method for evaluating scalar vacuum integrals on the D‑sphere by combining Schwinger‑parameterization, total‑derivative identities, and edge‑contraction relations into a solvable linear system. They solve all two‑loop vacuum graphs, including the three‑melon diagram, obtaining analytic expressions valid for arbitrary D and explicit dimensional‑regularized results at integer dimensions.

papers.title: TQFT gravity dual to the orbifold groupoid of Narain code CFTs over $\mathbb{Z}_4$
papers.authors: Rajae Sammani, Abdellah Sebbar
papers.abstract: In a companion paper arXiv:2610.26610, we classified the Narain conformal field theories obtained by gluing copies of the $A_3$ root and weight lattices along their $\mathbb{Z}_4$ discriminant group. For two hyperbolic pairs, this gives twenty-two even self-dual gluing codes, which fall into seven inequivalent theories at $c=\bar c=6$. In this paper, we develop the physical interpretation of this family and its connections to three-dimensional topological field theory. We show that all twenty-two codes are topological boundary conditions of a single abelian Chern-Simons theory. Its invertible symmetries, which include fractional $B$-field shifts, organize the boundaries into three orbits: free, mixed and torsion. Boundaries in different orbits are related only by gauging. We determine all gaugings of order at most four between the seven theories, by $\mathbb{Z}_2$, $\mathbb{Z}_4$ and $\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_2$, with explicit twisted partition functions, and follow their effect on the spectrum and the current algebra. We then sum the Chern-Simons partition function over handlebodies at genus one and prove a finite Siegel-Weil identity, valid for any number of pairs. For two pairs, the handlebody sum is the uniform average over the free theories. Recovering the average over all twenty-two theories requires one additional contribution, a solid torus with the torsion lines along its core. For three or more pairs, we find that the handlebody sum is not a positive combination of code boundary states.
papers.summary: The paper constructs a single abelian Chern–Simons theory whose topological boundary conditions realize all twenty‑two Narain CFTs obtained from gluing (A_3) lattices over (mathbb{Z}_4), and classifies their mutual gaugings by finite abelian groups, including explicit twisted partition functions. It then evaluates the handlebody sum of the Chern–Simons partition function at genus one, proving a finite Siegel–Weil identity and showing that for two lattice pairs the sum equals the uniform average over the free theories, while for more pairs the sum fails to be a positive combination of code boundary states.

papers.title: Beyond the Fock Vacuum in Finite-$N$ Bilocal Algebras of Vector Models
papers.authors: Byoungjoon Ahn, Robert de Mello Koch, Vatsal Garg, Antal Jevicki, Junggi Yoon
papers.abstract: We discuss the finite-$N$ Hilbert space of bilocal operators that underlies bilocal holography of vector models, beyond the sector built on the Fock vacuum. If the microscopic oscillator Fock space carries a multiplicity-free dual action of a compact color group $G$ and a bilocal algebra, Howe duality implies that projection to the derived subgroup $[G,G]$ selects precisely the characters of the abelianization $G^{\rm ab}=G/[G,G]$ that occur in the Fock space. Thus $O(N)/SO(N)=\mathbb Z_2$ gives two sectors, $U(N)/SU(N)=U(1)$ gives integer determinant-charge sectors, while $Sp(N)$ is perfect and gives no additional sector; Bose/Fermi statistics and the number of modes determine which sectors are actually realized. We construct the epsilon and determinant backgrounds that generate these sectors, together with their finite-$N$ constraints and Casimirs, and find that the two bosonic $O(N)$ sectors are not distinguished by any Casimir. Using group-integral projectors, we derive explicit sector-resolved characters for the $O(N)$ and $U(N)$ theories. Around each new background we solve the constraints with auxiliary oscillators, which form a Fermi sea for bosonic matter. In the free vector model on $\mathbb R\times S^2$ the new sectors consist of baryonic primaries; we determine their energies, degeneracies and spin content exactly at finite $N$, together with their lowest energy at fixed angular momentum.
papers.summary: The paper extends the finite‑N Hilbert space of bilocal operators in vector models beyond the Fock vacuum, classifying new sectors via Howe duality and group‑theoretic projections. It constructs explicit epsilon and determinant backgrounds, computes their Casimirs, and determines the exact spectrum of baryonic primaries on $mathbb R	imes S^2$, offering new insights for bilocal holography.

papers.title: A periodic $\bar q$ equation for form factors
papers.authors: Song He, Jiahao Liu
papers.abstract: MHV form factors of the chiral stress-tensor multiplet in planar $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang-Mills theory are dual to periodic null Wilson loops. We propose a periodic $\bar q$ equation for the MHV and higher-helicity sectors at vanishing fermionic monodromy. The equation relates kinematic derivatives of $\mathrm N^k\mathrm{MHV}$ form factors to collinear integrals of $\mathrm N^{k+1}\mathrm{MHV}$ form factors with one additional external particle, providing a recursive relation in loop order. In periodic momentum supertwistors, it has the same collinear-integral form as the two dotted components of the amplitude $\bar Q$ equation, with coefficient $\Gamma_{\rm cusp}/4$, despite the absence of ordinary dual conformal invariance at fixed operator momentum. For parity-even scalar MHV remainders, combining the equation with its parity image supplies all directions of the kinematic differential.   We verify the equation analytically for the one-loop four-point NMHV form factor and reconstruct the two-loop three-point MHV remainder at function level. Further two-loop MHV tests give numerical agreement with derivatives of the known four-point remainder at a fixed kinematic configuration, and for five points, all six chiral derivatives agree exactly at symbol level for a one-parameter family of kinematics. The structure of the collinear source further gives all-loop predictions for MHV last entries, consistent with known results and form a space of dimension $n(2n-5)$. The periodic Wilson-loop picture also motivates an all-loop derivation. Using the form-factor OPE, we extract the one-loop correction to the fermion energy from the logarithmic source and recover its vanishing at zero momentum.
papers.summary: The paper develops a periodic β̄ equation that recursively relates derivatives of N^kMHV form factors to collinear integrals of higher-helicity sectors, providing analytic checks up to two loops and all-loop predictions for MHV last entries. It leverages a periodic Wilson-loop picture and the form-factor OPE to extract fermion energy corrections, offering a new tool for studying form factors in planar Δ=4 SYM.

papers.title: Surface Defects in the $\mathcal{N}=2$ Lens Space Index and Elliptic Integrability
papers.authors: Masahito Yamazaki
papers.abstract: We determine the surface-defect difference operators of the 4d $\mathcal{N}=2$ lens space index for class $\mathcal{S}$ theories of type $A_{N-1}$ on $(\mathbb{S}^3/\mathbb{Z}_r)\times\mathbb{S}^1$. For generic fugacities $(p,q,t)$ and arbitrary rank $N$, orbifold order $r$ and discrete holonomies, their coefficients are finite products of theta functions with nomes $p^r$ and $q^r$. After an explicit gauge transformation, Gaussian in the holonomies, each operator factorizes into two elliptic Ruijsenaars--Schneider-type operators with step $pq$, one with nome $p^r$ and one with nome $q^r$, acting on variables glued along a lattice. Using this factorization and a Wronski-type relation, we prove that all the operators commute. We also establish a sufficient criterion for self-adjointness with respect to the bilinear vector multiplet pairing. It applies to the basic mixed operator and, in suitable parameter chambers, to the pure $p$- and $q$-type operators; for general mixed operators the contour prescription remains open. These results support the expectations from S-duality.
papers.summary: This work constructs and analyzes difference operators that encode surface defects in the 4d N=2 lens space index for class S theories of type A_{N‑1}. By factorizing these operators into elliptic Ruijsenaars–Schneider pieces and proving their commutativity, the authors provide evidence for S‑duality and establish criteria for self‑adjointness, thereby extending the integrable structure underlying the index.

papers.title: Inverse KLT kernel of AdS string-amplitude building blocks from the intersection matrix
papers.authors: Yi-xiao Tao, Shijie Zhang
papers.abstract: We develop a topological and combinatorial interpretation of the Kawai--Lewellen--Tye (KLT) relations for $n$-point AdS string-amplitude building blocks, which are disk integrals with multivariable multiple polylogarithm insertions and sphere integrals with their single-valued counterparts. Building on the framework of twisted de Rham theory over a noncommutative ring, we reformulate the problem in terms of associahedral chambers of the moduli space loaded with solutions of the Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov equation. We construct regularized twisted cycles and express their intersection pairings through local monodromies and Drinfeld associators, which control transport between fusion-tree normalizations. Organizing the intersection contributions by common boundary faces yields the intersection matrix, which is identified with the inverse KLT kernel by the twisted period relation. The field-theory limit of the inverse KLT kernel is also given.
papers.summary: The paper develops a topological and combinatorial framework for Kawai–Lewellen–Tye (KLT) relations in AdS string amplitudes, using twisted de Rham theory, associahedral chambers, and Drinfeld associators to construct an intersection matrix that serves as the inverse KLT kernel, and it also provides its field‑theory limit. This work offers new tools for understanding multi‑point AdS string scattering and their connections to twisted periods and monodromy data.

papers.title: Phases of flux vacua and their quantum symmetries
papers.authors: Dan Israel, Ilarion V. Melnikov, Yann Proto
papers.abstract: We present a torsional linear sigma model with (0,2) supersymmetry that realizes, in its large radius phase, a five-dimensional heterotic flux vacuum, and we use the linear sigma model to connect this geometry to a stringy regime realized as an asymmetric orbifold of a Gepner model and a circle. Along the way we develop a number of tools relevant for more general (0,2) gauged linear sigma model constructions of heterotic vacua.
papers.summary: This paper constructs a torsional (0,2) linear sigma model that flows in the large radius limit to a five‑dimensional heterotic flux vacuum, and shows how this geometry can be connected to a stringy regime described by an asymmetric orbifold of a Gepner model and a circle. The authors develop tools for general (0,2) GLSM constructions of heterotic vacua, providing a bridge between geometric and orbifold descriptions.

papers.title: Quasinormal modes, complex null geodesics and singularity resolution in regular AdS black holes
papers.authors: Heng-Yu Chen, Yasuaki Hikida, Yasutaka Koga
papers.abstract: The black hole singularity is hidden behind its horizon, and it is difficult to determine whether it is resolved by quantum gravity or stringy effects. For an AdS-Schwarzschild black hole, it is known that the two-point function of the dual conformal field theory has a singularity associated with a null geodesic that bounces off the black hole singularity. In this paper, we investigate how the resolution of the black hole singularity is encoded in the dual conformal field theory by considering regular AdS black holes as regularized geometries. Using WKB analysis, we compute the quasinormal modes of regular AdS black holes and read off the dual two-point functions from the modes. We find that the singularity corresponding to the bouncing null geodesic for singular black holes is replaced by a smooth bump associated with a complex, rather than real, null geodesic. The location of the complex geodesic singularity is supported by analyzing the structure of the operator product expansion for the two-point function. Our results provide a holographic signature of black hole singularity resolution and clarify how information about the regular interior is encoded in boundary correlation functions.
papers.summary: The authors compute quasinormal modes of regular AdS black holes via WKB and use them to reconstruct boundary two‑point functions, showing that the singularity from a real null geodesic is replaced by a smooth bump associated with a complex null geodesic. This provides a holographic signature of interior regularization and links the bulk singularity resolution to analytic structure of CFT correlators.

papers.title: Five-loop static two-body potential in massless scalar-tensor gravity
papers.authors: Gabriel Luz Almeida, Zhengwen Liu, Jia Zhang
papers.abstract: We compute the static contribution to the conservative two-body potential in massless scalar-tensor theories through fifth post-Newtonian (5PN) order, with the strong-field scalar responses of the compact objects encoded in scalar-dependent masses. Within post-Newtonian effective field theory (EFT), evaluating the 1PN-5PN static terms requires one- through five-loop massless two-point Feynman integrals. Although the additional scalar modifies both source couplings and integrand numerators, the required scalar master topologies remain those of the corresponding static problem in general relativity. Moreover, independent reflection symmetries of the two static scalar sectors extend the odd-PN factorization mechanism to the present theory, so that no genuinely new five-loop master integrals are required. Our results reproduce the known static interaction through 2PN, provide an independent EFT determination at 3PN, and extend the explicit potential to 4PN and 5PN. We verify the general-relativity limit and body-exchange symmetry; regulator poles and residual transcendental terms cancel in the complete result, leaving rational coefficients. These high-precision results provide ingredients for increasingly precise gravitational-wave tests of gravity beyond general relativity.
papers.summary: This paper computes the static two-body potential in massless scalar-tensor gravity up to fifth post-Newtonian order using EFT techniques, reproducing known results up to 2PN and extending them to 4PN and 5PN. The authors show that no new five-loop master integrals are needed and that the final potential has rational coefficients, providing precise inputs for gravitational-wave tests beyond general relativity.

papers.title: Small black hole in de Sitter as an observer
papers.authors: Guanda Lin, Haifeng Tang
papers.abstract: We study the Euclidean path integral around magnetically charged lukewarm black holes in four-dimensional de Sitter space. We numerically determine the full one-loop spectrum of coupled graviton and photon fluctuations and find that the phase of the partition function agrees with that of pure gravity in empty de Sitter plus a worldline observer. In the small-mass limit, certain localized eigenmodes can be effectively viewed as describing the observer's motion and have the expected eigenvalues, allowing us to reconstruct the worldline action. We further identify these modes with translational zero modes of an extremal charged black hole in asymptotically flat spacetime, lifted by de Sitter curvature.
papers.summary: The authors compute the one-loop spectrum of graviton and photon fluctuations around magnetically charged lukewarm black holes in 4d de Sitter, showing that the phase of the partition function matches that of empty de Sitter plus a worldline observer. In the small-mass limit they identify localized eigenmodes as the observer’s motion, reconstructing the worldline action and relating them to translational zero modes of an extremal charged black hole in flat space lifted by de Sitter curvature.

papers.title: Holographic surface defect RG flows without supersymmetry
papers.authors: Jos\'e Manuel Pen\'in, James Ratcliffe, Ronnie Rodgers, Dimitrios Zoakos
papers.abstract: We consider $\mathcal{N}=4$ supersymmetric Yang--Mills theory with gauge group SU$(N)$, which admits families of conformal surface defects defined by singular boundary conditions for scalar fields that completely break supersymmetry. At large $N$ and strong coupling, these defects are holographically dual either to a probe D5-brane or to one of two new D7-brane embeddings that we introduce in this work. We also construct embeddings of both D5- and D7-branes describing defect renormalisation group (RG) flows, for which the ultraviolet and infrared fixed points are both dual to the same D$p$-brane, with different values of a parameter. Our embeddings dual to RG flows are mostly constructed numerically, but we find a regime in which we can derive approximate analytic embeddings using a controlled perturbative expansion. We demonstrate that the $b$-theorem is satisfied by all of the RG flows that we study.
papers.summary: This paper studies non-supersymmetric surface defects in N=4 SYM and constructs their holographic duals as probe D5- and D7-brane embeddings, including numerical and analytic RG flow solutions. It verifies the b-theorem for these flows, providing new insights into defect CFT dynamics at strong coupling.

papers.title: Timelike Supersymmetric Geometries in Seven-Dimensional Supergravity
papers.authors: Mich\`ele Levi
papers.abstract: Seven-dimensional supergravity poses a uniquely intricate supersymmetry problem, combining topologically massive higher-form gauge dynamics, distinct Clifford algebra properties, and rich geometric structures. We first establish the complete formulation of the maximal Cartan-gauged theory in terms of the gauge-invariant higher-form flux, including both the bosonic action and supersymmetry variations. This formulation, which also makes the smooth ungauged limit manifest, is achieved by requiring a consistent truncation to the minimal Cartan-gauged theory in the equal-charge limit. We construct the complete bilinear system for a timelike Killing vector, where additional internal orientation of the symplectic-Majorana spinor arises already in the scalar sector, uniquely among pure minimal ungauged theories. In the equal-charge sector, we decouple the algebraic constraints into SU$(3)$-isotypic components, and analyse the differential bilinear relations, determining the permitted dilaton gradient, fluxes, fibration twist and intrinsic torsion of the base. We prove that with gauging and active Cartan flux, the complex scalar bilinear vanishes identically. We also construct a Killing gauge for the higher-form potential compatible with the self-duality condition. We show that with gauging but no active Cartan flux, the Killing vector also acts as a generator of the gauged R-symmetry, and the base structure is enlarged from SU$(3)$ to U$(3)$. We find that BPS-flow solutions realize this setting. With supersymmetry, we isolate a single independent component of the 3-form equation across an exhaustive four-class partition for both theories within this setup. Applied to known and proposed solutions in both theories, this classification exposes unexplored sectors and provides an accessible toolbox for constructing and testing solutions and developing new geometric and holographic applications.
papers.summary: This paper presents a complete formulation of the maximal Cartan-gauged seven‑dimensional supergravity, deriving the full bilinear system for timelike Killing vectors and classifying the resulting supersymmetric geometries. It identifies new BPS‑flow solutions, clarifies the role of Cartan flux and R‑symmetry, and offers a framework for constructing holographic backgrounds and exploring their geometric structure.

papers.title: String Amplitudes on Integer Rectangles
papers.authors: Song He, Yong Zhang, Fan Zhu, Pengfei Zhu
papers.abstract: Hidden zeros of tree-level string amplitudes of colored scalars lie on loci specified by integer-valued dimensionless momentum contractions arranged in rectangles on the kinematic mesh. We study the same kinematic loci for open-string amplitudes with gluons, fermions and higher-spin states at arbitrary finite mass levels. Disk monodromy relations yield $\textit{zero-locus factorization}$: at regular points where the monodromy system is invertible, the amplitude is a weighted sum of physical three-point amplitudes sewn to complete on-shell $(n-1)$-point amplitudes. Hidden zeros follow when the external wavefunctions annihilate all contributing three-point couplings. In the low-energy limit, the massless zero-integer branch recovers the corresponding field-theory factorization. For closed strings, including gravitons, persistent cubic zeros in both chiral sectors remove the disk poles, allowing the Kawai--Lewellen--Tye momentum-kernel zero to imply amplitude zeros. The operator product expansions of external vertices give a common worldsheet origin for these conditions across spins and mass levels.
papers.summary: The paper investigates hidden zeros of tree-level string amplitudes for colored scalars, gluons, fermions, and higher-spin states, showing that these zeros arise from monodromy relations and factorization into three-point couplings. It extends the analysis to closed strings, demonstrating how Kawai–Lewellen–Tye momentum-kernel zeros lead to amplitude zeros and provides a worldsheet origin for these conditions across spins and mass levels.

papers.title: High precision black hole scattering
papers.authors: Benjamin Sauer
papers.abstract: In this thesis we compute the impulse of a classical black hole scattering encounter in the Post-Minkowskian (PM) expansion - a weak-field expansion in Newton's constant $G$ - up to the fifth order. We describe the black holes as point particles within an effective field theory framework and couple them through gravity. The classical equations of motion are solved diagrammatically using the worldline quantum field theory (WQFT) formalism, in which the solution with causal boundary conditions is encoded in tree-level Feynman diagrams built from graviton and worldline fields. The Feynman integrals arising at each order are reduced by advanced IBP reduction techniques and evaluated with the method of differential equations. We find that, in the solution of these integrals, periods over Calabi--Yau manifolds - familiar from string theory - appear and contribute to the classical impulse at the fifth Post-Minkowskian order. The results of this work are the first analytic results for the scattering observables at fifth Post-Minkowskian order, together with the appearance of Calabi--Yau threefold periods in a classical physics observable.
papers.summary: This paper computes the classical impulse for a black‑hole scattering encounter to fifth Post‑Minkowskian order using worldline quantum field theory and advanced IBP/differential‑equation techniques. It reveals the first analytic appearance of Calabi–Yau threefold periods in a classical gravitational observable.

papers.title: Monodromy Defects of 3D Wilson-Fisher Criticality on the Fuzzy Sphere
papers.authors: Yin Tang, W. Zhu
papers.abstract: Monodromy (twist) line defects arise as the boundaries of topological symmetry surfaces, which are among the simplest non-trivial conformal defects with direct realizations as magnetic vortex in quantum magnets, as Wilson and t Hooft lines of gauge theories, and as the replica twist operators in quantum information theory. However, their interacting dynamics remains difficult to characterize non-perturbatively. Here we design a way to realize the monodromy boundary conditions in the fuzzy-sphere regularization by threading a symmetry-selective Aharonov-Bohm flux through the two poles of the sphere. We apply this construction to the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ twist of the 3D Ising conformal field theory (CFT), $\pi$-twist of the 3D O(2) CFT and three inequivalent monodromies of O(3) (centre twist, z-axis $\pi$-twist and the reflection). For each defect, we extract the low-lying defect spectrum together with bulk-to-defect and defect-defect operator product expansion coefficients, which characterize the operators living on the defect line, their mutual interactions, and how they couple to the surrounding critical bulk. Among the low-lying defect primaries resolved in our spectra, we find no relevant scalar perturbation that preserves all the symmetries of the corresponding defect. The relevant deformations identified in our calculations break at least one preserved symmetry, providing evidence that these monodromy defects are stable against symmetry-preserving relevant perturbations. These results establish a systematic set of non-perturbative conformal data for monodromy defects beyond the Ising twist. Our construction therefore turns the symmetry flux into a tunable knob of the fuzzy-sphere regularization, opening a route to exploring the response of critical matter to distinct defects.
papers.summary: This work introduces a fuzzy-sphere regularization that implements monodromy (twist) line defects by threading symmetry-selective Aharonov-Bohm fluxes through the poles, enabling non-perturbative extraction of defect spectra and OPE data for the 3D Ising, O(2), and O(3) CFTs. The results demonstrate stability of these defects under symmetry-preserving relevant perturbations and provide a systematic set of conformal data beyond the Ising twist.

papers.title: Exact stress-tensor generators distinguish integrable continuations
papers.authors: H. Babaei-Aghbolagh, Song He, Zahra Pezhman
papers.abstract: The same leading $T\bar T$ interaction can coexist with sharply different strong-field responses, even within causal, classically integrable sigma models. We reconstruct exact autonomous stress-tensor generators for prescribed one-scale Courant--Hilbert families in two dimensions. Separating the invariant stress scale from a signed trace ratio reduces reconstruction to one scalar inversion on each invertible physical branch. The resulting profile determines both the deformation law and the relation between local energy density and pressure. For generalized Born--Infeld and logarithmic models, the leading interactions coincide, yet pressure saturates in the former and grows without bound in the latter. Their exact generators are respectively quadratic and nonpolynomial, the latter involving Lambert $W_{-1}$. A regular Legendre transformation gives the same profile in the auxiliary potential formulation. The flows commute locally with root-$T\bar T$ within a common smooth branch and retain a common classical Lax form. Exact reconstruction thus quantifies the nonlinear freedom left by leading-order matching.
papers.summary: The paper constructs exact stress‑tensor generators for two‑dimensional integrable sigma models with a single deformation scale, showing that the same leading T ar T interaction can lead to very different strong‑field behaviours in Born‑Infeld versus logarithmic models. It demonstrates that the deformation law and the energy–pressure relation are encoded in a single scalar inversion, and that the resulting flows commute with root‑T ar T and preserve a common Lax pair.

papers.title: Unitarity methods for Magnus amplitudes
papers.authors: Jung-Wook Kim, Sungsoo Kim, Jian-Rong Li
papers.abstract: Magnus amplitudes refer to the matrix elements of the logarithm of the $S$-matrix. Modern unitarity methods construct cut-constructible parts of scattering amplitudes without directly invoking Feynman diagrams, offering an efficient way of obtaining loop integrands for scattering amplitudes. A procedure is presented that adapts unitarity methods to the computation of Magnus amplitudes.
papers.summary: The paper develops a technique to compute Magnus amplitudes—matrix elements of the logarithm of the S‑matrix—using modern unitarity methods that bypass explicit Feynman diagram calculations. It adapts cut‑constructible integrand construction to the logarithmic representation of scattering amplitudes, offering a more efficient loop‑level evaluation framework.

papers.title: The classical two-loop amplitude at leading logarithmic accuracy for graviton emission in multi-Regge kinematics
papers.authors: Federico Buccioni, Vittorio Del Duca, Emanuele Rosi
papers.abstract: Using the gravitational shockwave formalism, we compute the classical part of the $\mathcal{O}(G^{7/2})$ five-point amplitude at leading logarithmic accuracy describing the emission of a graviton in the collision of two massless scalars in multi-Regge kinematics (MRK). The result splits into a two-particle reducible term and a three-particle reducible one, the latter being the radiative counterpart of the $H$-diagram with the emission taken in MRK limit. The same amplitude can be equivalently calculated as the ultrarelativistic limit of the corresponding massive amplitude by applying the optical theorem according to the conjectured universality of the leading logarithmic amplitudes in classical gravity.
papers.summary: The authors compute the classical part of the five‑point amplitude at (mathcal{O}(G^{7/2})) in the multi‑Regge limit, splitting it into two‑ and three‑particle reducible pieces. They further demonstrate that the same result follows from the ultrarelativistic limit of the massive amplitude via the optical theorem, supporting the conjectured universality of leading‑logarithmic amplitudes in classical gravity.

papers.title: Krylov Complexity and Entropy of Composite Quantum Systems
papers.authors: Jeff Murugan, Victor Van Aswegen, Hendrik J R Van Zyl
papers.abstract: We investigate the behaviour of Krylov complexity as the number of degrees of freedom of a quantum system increases. Specifically, we show that for tensor products of commuting subsystems, the leading excess complexity is controlled by a weighted variance of the subsystem Lanczos coefficients. This provides a quantitative measure of dynamical heterogeneity and a precise characterization of synchronous evolution. We also show that Krylov entropy is able to disambiguate the information associated with subsystems composition from that generated by dynamical mismatch, and that the same Lanczos variance controls the leading mismatch contribution to both complexity and the entropy. Our results establish excess complexity and Krylov entropy as complementary probes of the emergence of collective dynamics in large quantum systems.
papers.summary: The paper studies how Krylov complexity scales with the number of degrees of freedom in composite systems, showing that for commuting tensor products the excess complexity is governed by a weighted variance of Lanczos coefficients, which also controls the leading mismatch contribution to Krylov entropy. These results provide quantitative tools for detecting collective dynamics and distinguishing subsystem composition from dynamical mismatch in large quantum systems.

papers.title: The Spectral Edge at Large Central Charge and Black Hole Statistics
papers.authors: Eric Perlmutter
papers.abstract: We introduce a new approach to high-energy spectra in AdS$_3$/CFT$_2$, addressing the open challenge of incorporating spectral statistics into the modular bootstrap. Using the analytic theory of $L$-functions attached to two-dimensional CFTs, we leverage modular constraints among high-energy states to derive a sum rule relating the spectral edge to bulk spectral fluctuations. As an application, we establish a refined modular bootstrap bound: letting $\Delta_1$ be the conformal dimension of the lightest excited Virasoro primary of a unitary CFT of central charge $c$, we show that $\Delta_1 - {c-1\over 12} \leq o(c)$, with at most one exceptional value of the scalar gap at each sufficiently large $c$; moreover, along any sequence in $c$ for which such exceptional gaps are realized, the remaining gaps obey the stronger bound $\Delta_1 - {c-1\over 12} \leq O(1)$. The result applies to theories with logarithmic rigidity of spectral counting fluctuations, as in random matrix theory.
papers.summary: This paper develops a modular bootstrap framework that incorporates spectral statistics via L‑functions, deriving a sum rule linking the spectral edge to bulk fluctuations in AdS$_3$/CFT$_2$. It yields a refined bound on the lightest primary gap, showing it stays within $O(1)$ of the BTZ threshold for almost all large central‑charge theories, with at most one exceptional gap per $c$.

papers.title: Exact Two-Loop Effective Potentials in de Sitter Space via Finite-Difference Methods
papers.authors: Bruce Bassett, Sergio Luigi Cacciatori, Ugo Moschella
papers.abstract: We compute the renormalised two-loop effective potential of the $O(N)$-symmetric scalar theory on four-dimensional de Sitter space. The main technical ingredient is the two-loop watermelon vacuum integral. Although a closed-form representation of this integral was previously available, extracting its finite part near four dimensions remained exceedingly difficult. We use exact finite-difference equations in the propagator spectral labels to obtain a representation in which the ultraviolet poles are isolated in Gamma-function factors and the remaining series are regular near four dimensions. We prove the boundary condition selecting the physical solution, extract the finite part, and combine the result with the tadpole reconstruction of the potential. The calculation includes the subtraction of subdivergences and the derivation of the matter-sector renormalisation-group functions. Holding the field-dependent masses and scalar curvature fixed makes the spectral labels regulator-dependent. We track this dependence explicitly and show that its derivative terms cancel after the forest subtraction. The resulting potential is exact in the mass-to-curvature ratios at two-loop order, away from propagator poles and subject to the usual limitations of perturbation theory. This is the first exact two-loop determination of the effective potential in four-dimensional de Sitter space.
papers.summary: The authors compute the renormalised two-loop effective potential for an O(N)-symmetric scalar theory in four-dimensional de Sitter space, using finite-difference equations to isolate UV poles and extract the finite part of the watermelon vacuum integral. Their method yields an exact potential in mass-to-curvature ratios, including proper subtraction of subdivergences and RG functions, marking the first such two-loop determination in de Sitter.

papers.title: Large $N$ hadron scattering bootstrap: massive pions and glueballs
papers.authors: Sebastiano Bocchia, Andrea Guerrieri
papers.abstract: We extend the large $N$ bootstrap of pion scattering to nonzero pion mass, and apply the same formalism to glueball scattering. Our bounds apply to Taylor coefficients and on-shell couplings of the exact planar amplitude. They do not rely on a truncated chiral expansion, so we can follow them as the quark mass varies, and apply them to glueballs, for which no low-energy effective theory exists. For pions, we bound the $O(p^4)$ coefficients and the $\pi\pi f_2$ coupling. As in the chiral limit, the bound on the $\pi\pi f_2$ coupling features a kink, where the extracted spectrum closely resembles the real-world meson spectrum. For glueballs, we bound the couplings of the lightest scalar glueball to heavier glueballs of higher spin, using the large $N$ lattice spectrum as input, and find extremal solutions with linear Regge trajectories.
papers.summary: This work extends large‑N bootstrap techniques to massive pions and glueball scattering, providing rigorous bounds on Taylor coefficients and on‑shell couplings without relying on a truncated chiral expansion. The analysis reveals a kink in the ππf₂ coupling bound that reproduces the real‑world meson spectrum and identifies extremal glueball solutions with linear Regge trajectories.

papers.title: Quantum gravity on the bulk cone
papers.authors: Ahmed Almheiri, Matthew Dodelson, Zohar Komargodski
papers.abstract: Bulk-cone singularities in holographic correlators encode propagation along bulk null geodesics. The prototypical example is an AdS black hole, where incoming null geodesics can wind around the photon sphere and return to the boundary. These singularities appear in real time in the thermal two-point function at finite volume. We show that conformal field theories dual to gravitational theories at finite $G_N$ cannot have such singularities. We rule out these singularities both for individual microstates and for the thermal state. The main thrust of the argument is to invoke an analytic continuation in the temperature. As a microscopic example, we construct an AdS$_3$ geometry with two colliding shocks which exhibits a bulk cone singularity. We show by an explicit calculation in the CFT that this singularity is smoothed out at finite $G_N$. Qualitatively, the singularity resolution is a consequence of the fuzziness of the bulk solution in quantum gravity.
papers.summary: The paper shows that bulk-cone singularities, which arise from null geodesics in AdS black holes, cannot appear in CFT correlators at finite Newton constant, using an analytic continuation in temperature and a shock-wave example. This demonstrates that quantum gravity smooths out such singularities, implying a fuzziness of bulk geometries in holographic duals.

papers.title: On Born-Infeld-type higher-spin interactions and supersymmetry
papers.authors: Nikita Zaigraev
papers.abstract: We develop a simple Lorentz-covariant construction of the Born--Infeld-type cubic interactions $(s, s_1, s_2)$ of massless higher-spin fields with $s + s_1 + s_2$ derivatives in four-dimensiona flat space. For arbitrary spins $s \ge s_1 \ge s_2$, the vertex is formulated in terms of a conserved higher-spin current and its trace. In contrast to the famous Berends--Burgers--van Dam currents, these currents are constructed from higher-spin Weyl tensors of a single chirality, schematically $J \sim \partial C \partial C$. Starting with a general ansatz, we derive recurrence relations fixing the current coefficients, identify the unique non-trivial conserved current after eliminating trivial (fake) vertices, and show that in the range $s \le s_1 + s_2$ the interaction admits a manifestly gauge-invariant representation in terms of higher-spin Weyl tensors. The construction is then extended to $\mathcal{N}=1$ and $\mathcal{N}=2$ supersymmetry using the corresponding off-shell superfield formalisms. In the $\mathcal{N}=1$ case, we obtain the general conserved integer superspin $s$ supercurrent with manifest supersymmetry, which is bilinear in the Weyl supertensors of superspins $Y_1$ and $Y_2$. For identical superfields, $Y_1 = Y_2$, this supercurrent vanishes for odd $s$ and is in agreement with earlier results by Gates and Koutrolikos. In the $\mathcal{N}=2$ case, using harmonic superspace, we construct the principal higher-spin supercurrent whose coefficients are uniquely fixed by the conservation equations. In contrast to the $\mathcal{N}=0,1$ cases, for identical $\mathcal{N}=2$ superfields, the corresponding vertex does not vanish. The results provide a systematic framework for Born--Infeld-type higher-spin interactions and their supersymmetric extensions.
papers.summary: The paper constructs Lorentz‑covariant Born–Infeld–type cubic interactions for massless higher‑spin fields in four‑dimensional flat space, formulating the vertices via conserved higher‑spin currents built from single‑chirality Weyl tensors and extending the framework to (mathcal{N}=1,2) supersymmetry. It provides a systematic method for generating higher‑spin interaction vertices and their supersymmetric counterparts, with implications for higher‑spin gauge theories and potential holographic duals.

papers.title: Onsager Algebras and Lattice Fermions
papers.authors: Ioanna Kourkoulou, David Tong
papers.abstract: We study the exact Onsager algebra of free lattice fermions in staggered, Wilson, and overlap incarnations, working in both Hamiltonian and Euclidean formulations in four spacetime dimensions. In each case, we show that the exact lattice algebra emanates the full chiral symmetry of the low-energy theory: if there are $N$ massless Dirac fermions in the continuum, the Onsager algebra reduces to a $U(2N)$ chiral symmetry. The details of which generators are quantised or ultra-local differ between formulations. There is also a trade-off between the locality of generators and the maximum compact subgroup of the Onsager algebra.
papers.summary: This paper investigates the exact Onsager algebra underlying free lattice fermions in various discretizations and demonstrates that it reproduces the full U(2N) chiral symmetry of N massless Dirac fermions in the continuum. The authors analyze how different formulations trade locality of generators against the size of the compact subgroup, offering insights into lattice symmetry structures.

papers.title: Half-Completeness from Standard Gravitational Dispersion Relations
papers.authors: Lukas W. Lindwasser, Laurentiu Rodina, Justinas Rumbutis
papers.abstract: The completeness hypothesis states that quantum gravity realizes every representation allowed by its gauge group. Previous S-matrix arguments used the graviton pole to constrain exchanged representations, including a proof of completeness by imposing an additional high-energy bound on crossing-odd amplitudes. We investigate what follows without this assumption, using standard twice-subtracted dispersion relations, positivity, and crossing symmetry. For external massless SU(2) isospin $J$, we prove ``half-completeness'': either massive exchanges include every isospin $j\le J$, or at least one $j>J$ is required. At $J=1$, we construct an explicit amplitude with only $j=0,1$ exchanges that satisfies these conditions but violates the crossing-odd bound. This establishes that the additional high-energy assumption does not follow from the standard framework. For $J\ge2$, however, we show that lower-only spectra cannot be realized within a class of string-inspired Euler amplitudes, leaving their existence an open question. More generally, for scalar matter transforming under any compact internal symmetry group, we prove that massive singlets of unbounded Lorentz spin must be exchanged.
papers.summary: This paper reexamines the completeness hypothesis in quantum gravity by dropping the high‑energy crossing‑odd bound and using standard twice‑subtracted dispersion relations. It proves that for massless SU(2) isospin J either all lower isospins up to J appear in the massive spectrum or a higher isospin must be present, constructs a J=1 counterexample that satisfies positivity and crossing but violates the crossing‑odd bound, and leaves the existence of lower‑only spectra for J≥2 as an open question.

papers.title: Ricci flow of Integrable Sigma Models, Hitchin Systems and Quantum Seiberg-Witten theory
papers.authors: G. Bonelli, S. Lacroix, T. Pedroni, A. Tanzini
papers.abstract: We construct a family of integrable 2d sigma models through 4d Chern-Simons theory and show that their classical point-particle reduction corresponds to a Hitchin system. The integrable Hitchin quantisation then provides a natural candidate Hamiltonian for the one-loop reduced dynamics of the sigma models, which coincides with the Perelman operator in all cases examined. This allows us to study the corresponding spectral problems using 4d $\mathcal{N}=2$ gauge theory and 2d conformal field theory methods. For the sausage model, we derive exact quantisation conditions and compute exponentially small corrections essential for the agreement with numerical finite-volume results.
papers.summary: The authors construct integrable 2d sigma models via 4d Chern‑Simons theory and show that their classical reduction is a Hitchin system, whose quantum Hitchin quantisation yields a Hamiltonian matching the Perelman operator. Using 4d N=2 gauge theory and 2d CFT techniques they solve the spectral problem for the sausage model, obtaining exact quantisation conditions and exponentially small corrections that agree with finite‑volume numerics.

papers.title: Quantum Charge as a Particle/Antiparticle Label
papers.authors: Alexander D. Popov
papers.abstract: We show that the concept of particles and antiparticles is related to the Weyl-Heisenberg group $W\!H_3$. Its generators are the position operators $\hat x^a$, the momentum operators $\hat p_a$, and the central element $Q_{\sf{v}}$, which defines a subgroup U(1)$_{\sf v}$ of $W\!H_3$. We show that the wave functions have a charge relative to the group U(1)$_{\sf{v}}$ equal to either $q_+=1/\hbar$ (particle $\psi_+$) or $q_-=-1/\hbar$ (antiparticle $\psi_-$). We call these eigenvalues of the operator $Q_{\sf{v}}$ quantum charges: $Q_{\sf{v}}\psi_\pm^{}=q_\pm^{}\psi_\pm^{}$. The wave functions $\psi_+$ and $\psi_-$ belong to the Hilbert spaces $\mathcal{H}_+$ and $\mathcal{H}_-$, on which unitarily inequivalent representations $\pi_\hbar$ and $\pi_{-\hbar}$ of the Weyl-Heisenberg group $W\!H_3$ are defined. These representations are related to each other by the antilinear charge conjugation operator $\hat C$, which maps $\mathcal{H}_+, q_+$ to $\mathcal{H}_-, q_-$. Charges $q_\pm^{}$ are intrinsic characteristics of the wave functions $\psi_\pm^{}$, similar to spin and electric charge. The wave function possesses one of these charges, $q_+$ or $q_-$, prior to the specification of any equations. We show that negative probabilities/energies and the Klein paradox in Klein-Gordon and Dirac theories are consequences of the violation of U(1)$_{\sf v}$-invariance in these theories. Restoring this invariance separates particle and antiparticles and eliminates all paradoxes at the level of first-quantized relativistic theories.
papers.summary: This paper reinterprets the particle/antiparticle distinction as eigenvalues of a central U(1) generator in the Weyl–Heisenberg algebra, proposing that quantum charge is an intrinsic label that resolves the Klein paradox by enforcing U(1) invariance. It shows that the two inequivalent representations of the Weyl–Heisenberg group correspond to particle and antiparticle Hilbert spaces, linked by an antilinear charge conjugation operator.

papers.title: Alexander Torsion and Floer Comparisons in the BV-BFV Formalism
papers.authors: Nima Moshayedi
papers.abstract: We compare relative Abelian BF torsion with the Alexander-graded Euler characteristic of knot Floer homology. A meridional annulus boundary condition identifies the normalized relative torsion with the Alexander polynomial. One exact prime-cyclotomic torsion value recovers all its coefficients under a sharp genus bound, compatibly with connected-sum gluing and branched-cover formulas. We compute interface contractions and obstructions to scalar comparisons, including the pairing defect of two-sector reduction for the degree-zero torus algebra. A six-generator dg resolution yields an equivalence of perfect-module categories preserving derived pairings and admits a classical one-dimensional BV-BFV realization. In the fixed nonresonant polynomial quantum BFV sector, over characteristic zero with $\hbar$ inverted, both states and Weyl observables reduce to a vacuum field; a Hochschild invariant obstructs a Morita equivalence with the degree-zero torus algebra. These results do not establish a full geometric BV-BFV/Floer equivalence.
papers.summary: This paper studies the relationship between Abelian BF torsion and knot Floer homology within the BV‑BFV formalism, showing how relative torsion can be identified with the Alexander polynomial under specific boundary conditions. It also explores algebraic structures and obstructions in the BF‑BFV setting, but does not directly address holography or related amplitude computations.

papers.title: Neutrino Transition Polarizability
papers.authors: Matteo Borrello, Michele Tammaro
papers.abstract: We study Neutrino Transition Polarizability, where a light pseudoscalar $\phi$ couples active neutrinos to heavy neutral leptons $N$ and interacts with two photons. We consider an effective description of the active - sterile interaction, and a realization within the inverse seesaw mechanism; the coupling to photons is generated by heavy charged states. For $m_N>m_\phi$, the decay $N\to\nu\phi$ can greatly shorten the heavy neutrino lifetime, while $\phi\to\gamma\gamma$ produces a displaced photon pair. This changes the relevant search strategies, favoring production and decay inside detectors. We discuss existing constraints and estimate the sensitivity of displaced photon searches at DUNE, Belle II, LHCb and FCC-ee, highlighting the complementarity of neutrino scattering and meson and electroweak boson decays.
papers.summary: This paper investigates a light pseudoscalar that mediates interactions between active neutrinos and heavy neutral leptons, leading to rapid decays of the heavy neutrinos and displaced photon signatures. It evaluates current constraints and projects sensitivity for displaced photon searches at upcoming experiments such as DUNE, Belle II, LHCb, and FCC‑ee.

papers.title: Mass-Varying Dark Matter, Naturally
papers.authors: C\'edric Delaunay, Seung J. Lee, Yuan Yin, Bingrong Yu
papers.abstract: Ultralight scalars that vary dark-matter masses require protection from quantum corrections.
