Cyclic $\mathbb{Z}_N$ symmetries provide this protection but also suppress variation of the mean mass of equally populated partners. Unsuppressed variation typically requires asymmetric reheating through symmetry-breaking couplings that threaten radiative control. We show that scalar-induced mass splittings built into these constructions can instead bias relic abundances through symmetric interactions. The mechanism applies to thermal and nonthermal relics that reach internal equilibrium after production, and permits mass variation over a broad range of timescales.
papers.summary: The paper studies ultralight scalar fields that induce time‑dependent dark matter masses, employing cyclic ℤ_N symmetries to protect against quantum corrections while allowing mass variation via asymmetric reheating. It proposes that scalar‑induced mass splittings can bias relic abundances through symmetric interactions, applicable to both thermal and nonthermal relics that equilibrate internally.

papers.title: Ricci-flat Seeds, Trombone Rescaling and Magnetizing Kerr Black Holes
papers.authors: Liang Ma, H. Lu
papers.abstract: We present a new family of Ricci-flat rotating metrics, which we refer to as Solution II, obtained by demagnetizing the genuine Kerr-Bertotti-Robinson (G-KBR) black hole. Together with Solution I, which was previously obtained by demagnetizing the Kerr-Bertotti-Robinson (KBR) black hole, this gives two families of Ricci-flat deformations of the Kerr black hole, each labeled by $B$. We study the global structures, thermodynamics, various limits, and the local connections among these limits. We also study the remagnetizations in both Einstein-Maxwell and Kaluza-Klein theories, and find that, to yield a physically acceptable solution, the Ernst transformation should be augmented by an appropriate trombone rescaling.
papers.summary: We present two new families of Ricci-flat rotating metrics obtained by demagnetizing Kerr-Bertotti-Robinson black holes, exploring their global structure, thermodynamics, and remagnetization in Einstein–Maxwell and Kaluza–Klein theories, with a required trombone rescaling of the Ernst transformation. The work provides explicit deformations of the Kerr solution labeled by a magnetic parameter B, offering new exact solutions for rotating spacetimes.

papers.title: The deepest X-ray view of a kiloparsec scale jet at z=6.1
papers.authors: Fabio A. Meanti, Luca Ighina, Alberto Moretti, Kyra Bettwy, Alessandro Caccianiga, Thomas Connor, Fabrizio Tavecchio, Silvia Belladitta, Emmanuel K. Bempong-Manful, Cristiana Spingola
papers.abstract: The mechanism responsible for the high-energy emission observed in kiloparsec-scale jets across cosmic time remains poorly understood. The relativistic jet associated with the z=6.1 AGN PSO J030947.49+271757.31 is the highest-redshift large-scale jet currently resolved in X-rays, providing a unique opportunity to study these structures.   We present new Chandra observations, combined with archival data, for a total exposure of 360 ks. The increased exposure allowed us to resolve the extended X-ray emission into two distinct, slightly resolved components and perform spatially resolved spectral analyses.   The extended emission has a photon index of Gamma = 2.25 (+0.45, -0.44), steeper than that of the core (Gamma = 1.86 +/- 0.09), and an extended-to-core luminosity ratio of 18%. Simulations using the Chandra image as input show that an AXIS-like mission could increase the detected photon statistics by a factor of approximately 17.   We resolve the kiloparsec-scale jet into two main components and constrain its spectral properties. This is the most distant and one of the most X-ray-luminous large-scale jets currently known. Future X-ray missions with arcsecond-scale angular resolution could enable more detailed studies of such systems and reveal a population of fainter high-redshift jets beyond Chandra's reach.
papers.summary: This paper presents deep Chandra observations of the highest-redshift kiloparsec-scale jet, resolving its X-ray emission into two components and measuring their spectra. The results highlight the jet’s steep photon index and high extended-to-core luminosity ratio, offering a benchmark for future high-resolution X-ray missions.

papers.title: Thermomagnetic enhancement of conserved-charge correlations in a lattice-constrained PNJL model
papers.authors: Bruno S. Lopes, Arthur E. B. Pasqualotto, Jandir J. Buttenbender Filho, Dyana C. Duarte, Ricardo L. S. Farias
papers.abstract: Conserved-charge correlations offer a promising probe of magnetic fields in strongly interacting matter. We investigate their magnetic response and the finite-density equation of state within a lattice-constrained three-flavor Polyakov--Nambu--Jona-Lasinio model. A thermomagnetic scalar coupling, inferred by Gaussian process regression from lattice QCD results for the average light-quark condensate, incorporates inverse magnetic catalysis into the effective interaction. Without fitting conserved-charge observables, the resulting framework substantially improves their magnetic-field dependence and crossover behavior compared with the fixed-coupling model. In particular, it captures the pronounced magnetic enhancement of the baryon--electric-charge correlation and related susceptibility ratios, supporting their use as QCD magnetometers. The comparison demonstrates that the medium dependence of the effective interaction is essential to describe this response within the model. We further calculate pressure Taylor coefficients through sixth order and reconstruct the pressure and baryon density at nonzero baryon chemical potential. Our results show that lattice information from a single chiral observable constrains a broad thermodynamic response, connecting inverse magnetic catalysis, conserved-charge correlations, and the equation of state in a common framework. This provides a lattice-constrained basis for investigating magnetic-field signatures and finite-density thermodynamics in QCD matter.
papers.summary: This study extends a lattice-constrained PNJL model by incorporating a thermomagnetic scalar coupling derived from lattice QCD, thereby capturing inverse magnetic catalysis and accurately reproducing conserved-charge correlations under magnetic fields. The authors also compute high-order pressure Taylor coefficients, enabling reconstruction of the equation of state at finite baryon density, offering a unified framework for magnetic-field signatures in QCD thermodynamics.

papers.title: ULTRAMAN: A Proposed ultrasound detector for macroscopic dark matter
papers.authors: Oem Trivedi, Robert J. Scherrer, Alfredo Gurrola
papers.abstract: We propose ULTRAMAN (ULTRAsound Macro ANalyzer), a passive ultrasound array experiment designed to search for macroscopic dark matter (macros) through coherent acoustic disturbances generated as compact objects traverse a controlled target medium. Unlike existing dark matter detectors that primarily rely on scintillation, ionization, or other signatures of energy deposition, ULTRAMAN exploits the acoustic response of matter to reconstruct individual highly supersonic trajectories using synchronized multielement ultrasound arrays. The framework connects macro stopping power and interaction cross section to the resulting acoustic pressure, while the expected event rate probes the macro mass and abundance. A genuine candidate would appear not as an isolated radio frequency spike, but as a correlated multichannel track consistent with a single highly supersonic passage through the target. Representative macro, nuclearite, axion quark nugget, and primordial black hole benchmarks are shown to occupy distinct regions of the resulting acoustic observable space. Existing ultrasound technology offers a realistic route to an event-level terrestrial search for macroscopic dark matter, with null observations translating into complementary constraints on its parameter space.
papers.summary: ULTRAMAN proposes a passive ultrasound array to detect macroscopic dark matter via coherent acoustic disturbances as compact objects traverse a target medium, reconstructing supersonic trajectories from multichannel pressure signals. The study maps macro stopping power to acoustic pressure, offering event-level constraints on macro mass and abundance complementary to traditional dark matter searches.

papers.title: Localized Neutrinos in Two Dark Dimensions
papers.authors: Waqas Ahmed, George K. Leontaris
papers.abstract: We study neutrino masses in a six-dimensional framework with two compact dark dimensions. In the conventional flat-bulk realization, the sterile-neutrino zero mode is strongly volume suppressed, so a fundamental scale near $10~\mathrm{TeV}$ requires a large higher-dimensional Yukawa coupling to reproduce the observed neutrino masses, while the accompanying two-dimensional Kaluza--Klein tower is strongly constrained by oscillation data. We show that localizing the sterile-neutrino wave function near the Standard-Model brane substantially alleviates both effects. Using a Gaussian localizer, realistic Dirac neutrino masses are obtained with perturbative, order-one Yukawa couplings, while the brane-visible sterile excitations form a shell spectrum with $M_s^2=8\mu^2 s$, and squared active--sterile mixings that decrease as $1/s$. The localization scale therefore separates the experimentally relevant sterile-neutrino spectrum from the gravitational compactification scale. We derive the resulting three-flavour structure and study its phenomenological consequences for reactor oscillations and tritium beta decay, including comparisons with current flat-LED and KATRIN constraints.
papers.summary: The paper investigates Dirac neutrino masses in a six‑dimensional model with two compact dark dimensions, showing that localizing the sterile neutrino near the SM brane allows realistic masses with perturbative Yukawa couplings and a suppressed KK tower. It analyzes the resulting sterile spectrum, mixing patterns, and constraints from reactor data and KATRIN, contrasting with flat large extra dimension scenarios.

papers.title: Spin-Clifford Bundles and Spin Connections on the Hyperbolic Clifford Algebra - Part I
papers.authors: E. Notte-Cuello, J. M. Hoff da Silva
papers.abstract: We develop the theory of spinor fields associated with the hyperbolic Clifford algebra $\mathbb{R}^{H}=\mathcal{C}\ell(H_V)$, which is associated with hyperbolic space $H_V=V\oplus V^{*}$. Algebraically, we exhibit an explicit real primitive idempotent which, unlike the Lorentzian case, remains primitive after complexification and generates the ideal of Witten superfields. We also describe the chirality decomposition and the hyperbolic spin group. Geometrically, we construct a canonical hyperbolic spin structure on every oriented manifold, showing that no topological obstructions arise beyond orientability and we study the associated spinor bundles, spin-Clifford bundles and ideal spinor subbundles. Finally, we introduce the isotropic extension of an arbitrary linear connection to $TM\oplus T^*M$, which is always compatible with the hyperbolic metric, and the associated hyperbolic spin connection, whose well-definedness, compatibilities, curvature and explicit form are established, providing the geometric framework for Dirac operators on the hyperbolic Clifford algebra, which we will present in a forthcoming article.
papers.summary: The paper develops a comprehensive framework for spinor fields and spin connections on the hyperbolic Clifford algebra, constructing a canonical hyperbolic spin structure on any oriented manifold and defining compatible hyperbolic spin connections that enable Dirac operators in this setting. It also introduces an isotropic extension of arbitrary linear connections to the tangent-plus-cotangent bundle, providing a geometric foundation that could be useful for holographic and conformal field theory applications.

papers.title: Yukawa textures due to selection rules in magnetized orbifold models
papers.authors: Tatsuo Kobayashi, Tomoyasu Kori, Shuhei Miyamoto, Riku Nakano, Haruki Uchida
papers.abstract: We study systematically Yukawa textures, which can be derived from magnetized $T^2/\mathbf{Z}_2$ and $T^2/\mathbf{Z}_4$ orbifold models with various magnetic fluxes and Scherk-Schwarz phases. Remarkably, the nearest neighbor interaction pattern as well as the diagonal Yukawa matrix is statistically favorable in $T^2/\mathbf{Z}_2$ orbifold models. Also, in $T^2/\mathbf{Z}_4$ orbifold models, selection rules are nontrivial and lead to textures, which cannot be derived from group-theoretical symmetries.
papers.summary: The paper systematically analyzes Yukawa coupling textures arising from magnetized T^2/Z_2 and T^2/Z_4 orbifold compactifications, exploring how magnetic fluxes and Scherk–Schwarz phases impose selection rules. It finds that nearest-neighbor interaction patterns and diagonal Yukawa matrices are statistically favored in Z_2 models, while Z_4 models yield nontrivial textures not derivable from conventional group symmetries.

papers.title: Matter Induced Bounds: Photon Ring, Lyapunov Exponent, Induced Temperature
papers.authors: Hocheol Lee, Bogeun Gwak
papers.abstract: We investigate analytic bounds on the equatorial photon ring radius and the Lyapunov exponent in rotating black holes containing anisotropic matter. For a constant equatorial equation-of-state parameter, the finite asymptotic mass and nonnegative energy density imply an upper bound on the photon ring radius given by the Kerr photon ring radius with the same asymptotic mass and rotation parameters for co-rotating and counter-rotating motions. The lower bounds are written in terms of the quantities evaluated at the outer horizon. These bounds on the Lyapunov exponent constrain the absolute magnitude of the imaginary part of the quasinormal frequency of a massless scalar field within the eikonal limit. The worldsheet surface gravity and induced temperature were derived for a probe string in the Penrose limit along the photon ring. The induced temperature and worldsheet surface gravity give an upper bound on the photon ring Lyapunov exponent, $2 \pi T_\mathrm{ind} = \kappa_\mathrm{ind} \geq \lambda$.
papers.summary: The authors derive analytic bounds on the equatorial photon ring radius and Lyapunov exponent for rotating black holes with anisotropic matter, showing that the bounds are set by the Kerr values and horizon quantities. They also compute the induced temperature and worldsheet surface gravity for a probe string in the Penrose limit, linking the photon ring Lyapunov exponent to the induced temperature via an inequality.

papers.title: Constrain the number of inner horizons from gravitational Noether charges
papers.authors: Jing-Peng Ye, Run-Qiu Yang
papers.abstract: A central question in the study of black hole interiors is how matter and geometry constrain the number of horizons. In Einstein gravity, one known method is to use the ADM decomposition of the field equations to derive a differential inequality for the lapse, which then constrains the possible multiple inner horizons. We show that the same obstruction can instead be formulated through the Komar integral as a bulk-boundary balance of gravitational Noether charge. In higher-curvature gravity, a direct ADM analysis becomes more complicated, whereas the gravitational Noether charge naturally retains this bulk-boundary structure. We naturally apply the gravitational Noether charge analysis to Lovelock gravity. We introduce a TCC-like curvature condition and prove that, together with the thermodynamically motivated assumption of positive Wald entropy, it allows at most one nondegenerate inner Killing horizon inside a nondegenerate event horizon. This suggests that the obstruction reflects a compatibility between bulk gravitational response and horizon thermodynamics.
papers.summary: The paper shows that the number of inner horizons in a black hole is bounded by a bulk–boundary balance of gravitational Noether charge, extending a known ADM result to higher‑curvature theories. In Lovelock gravity, a TCC‑like curvature condition together with positive Wald entropy guarantees at most one nondegenerate inner Killing horizon inside a nondegenerate event horizon.

papers.title: Quantum Constrained Hamiltonian Descent
papers.authors: Yoshihiko Abe, Ryo Nagai
papers.abstract: We propose Quantum Constrained Hamiltonian Descent (QCHD), a continuous-time quantum framework for optimization under smooth equality constraints. The unconstrained counterpart, Quantum Hamiltonian Descent (QHD), minimizes a cost function by simulating the Schr\"odinger dynamics of a particle in the potential given by the cost function. Applying Dirac's formalism to the classical dynamics with constraints, we construct an intrinsic quantum Hamiltonian with a Laplace--Beltrami operator on the constraint manifold in a kinetic term. Its evolution preserves the constraints exactly without penalty terms and is expected to solve quantum-dynamically the constrained optimization problem. We analyze its relation to Quantum Hamiltonian Descent supplemented by a strong penalty term. For a squared-distance penalty, the effective tangential dynamics acquires an extrinsic-curvature potential and, in nontrivial normal-rotation sectors, a coupling to the normal-bundle connection. These embedding-dependent terms remain in the strong-penalty limit, generally yielding quantum dynamics different from QCHD. Numerical comparisons for circular, elliptical, and two simultaneous constraints show faster optimization and improved concentration near global minima for the initial states and finite penalty strengths considered.
papers.summary: This paper introduces QCHD, a quantum dynamics framework that enforces smooth equality constraints via Dirac's formalism, yielding a Laplace–Beltrami kinetic term on the constraint manifold. Numerical tests show faster convergence and better concentration near global minima compared to penalty-based quantum Hamiltonian descent.

papers.title: Gravitational waves from highly charged binary black holes in Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton theory
papers.authors: Ryoto Tomie, Kai Togashi, Kitaro Taniguchi, Ryotaro Kase
papers.abstract: We perform fully nonlinear numerical-relativity simulations of electrically charged binary black hole mergers in Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton (EMD) theory, varying the magnitude and relative sign of the input charges and the dilaton coupling $a$. In the weak-charge sequence, the dominant gravitational waveforms remain close to the neutral vacuum baseline of general relativity and are visually indistinguishable across the sampled couplings, consistent with earlier EMD simulations. For the highly charged binaries with equal-magnitude opposite charges, however, the dominant gravitational strain exhibits visible differences between the EMD cases with $a\neq0$ and the charged Einstein-Maxwell reference at $a=0$. At $a=1$, the coordinate-time interval from the same separation to the waveform-based merger is approximately $62\%$ shorter than for the neutral binary. In this high-charge sequence at fixed input charges, increasing $a$ strengthens the scalar dressing while leaving the individual dilaton-weighted horizon charges nearly unchanged. Within the same sequence, increasing $a$ across the sampled values decreases the dipolar electromagnetic-flux peak, increases the scalar-flux peak, and modestly lengthens the merger interval. The sampled like-charged binaries have corresponding merger intervals approximately $15\%$-$20\%$ longer than the neutral baseline and emit predominantly quadrupolar electromagnetic radiation. At $a=1$ and $a=\sqrt{3}$, the like-charged mergers leave charged remnants with scalar fields consistent with secondary dilaton hair. The opposite-charge remnants instead approach neutral black holes without stationary scalar hair.
papers.summary: This study presents fully nonlinear numerical-relativity simulations of electrically charged binary black hole mergers in Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton theory, exploring how varying the dilaton coupling and charge configurations affect gravitational and electromagnetic waveforms. The results show that highly charged, opposite-charge binaries exhibit significant deviations from GR, while like-charged systems produce longer merger times and predominantly quadrupolar electromagnetic radiation, with remnants displaying secondary dilaton hair for certain couplings.

papers.title: Hadamard states for linearized gravity on asymptotically flat spacetimes
papers.authors: Christian G\'erard, Mikhail Molodyk, Micha{\l} Wrochna
papers.abstract: We consider the quantization of linearized Einstein equations on 4-dimensional asymptotically flat spacetimes. We prove the existence of fully gauge invariant Hadamard states in the harmonic gauge for any Einstein metric asymptotic to the Minkowski metric in a conic neighborhood of spatial infinity.
papers.summary: The paper establishes the existence of fully gauge‑invariant Hadamard states for linearized Einstein equations on 4‑dimensional asymptotically flat spacetimes, proving that any Einstein metric asymptotic to Minkowski in a conic neighborhood of spatial infinity admits such states in harmonic gauge. This result provides a rigorous foundation for quantizing linearized gravity in asymptotically flat backgrounds, with implications for the study of quantum gravitational observables at null infinity.

papers.title: Charmed baryon-to-meson ratios inside jets as a discriminator of hadronization mechanisms: from color reconnection in p+p to coalescence in Pb+Pb
papers.authors: Zi-Xuan Xu, Wei Dai, Ben-Wei Zhang, Enke Wang
papers.abstract: Jets separate the products of hard scatterings from the underlying event and thus help to clarify the origin of the enhanced baryon-to-meson ratios observed from small to large collision systems. We investigate the charmed baryon-to-meson ratio $\Lambda_c^+/D^0$ within jets in p+p and Pb+Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=5.02$~TeV to discriminate between candidate hadronization mechanisms. In p+p collisions, simulated with PYTHIA8 using color reconnection (CR-BLC Mode 2) as a representative beyond-leading-color scenario, the in-jet ratio is enhanced at low-to-intermediate $p_T$ relative to the inclusive one---opposite to the light-flavor $\Lambda/K^0_S$ case---because the color-reconnection-induced excess of the ratio remains correlated with the jet and survives the jet requirement, while the fragmentation baseline shows no such enhancement. In Pb+Pb collisions, described by the SHELL model with a coalescence plus fragmentation hybrid hadronization, the in-jet ratio is instead suppressed moderately at intermediate $p_T$, because coalescence hadrons assembled from soft thermal partons carry no correlation with the jet direction and are preferentially discarded by the jet selection. The sign of the in-jet modification thus discriminates between the two mechanisms. Both mechanisms shift charmed hadrons toward small values of the parallel jet momentum fraction $z^{ch}_{||}$, with a stronger effect on $\Lambda_c^+$, so that the $z^{ch}_{||}$ spectrum probes non-fragmentation hadronization independently of parton energy loss. The radial profile of the in-jet ratio rises with the distance from the jet axis in both systems, with the lowest-$p_T$ interval displaced farthest for color reconnection and the intermediate-$p_T$ interval for coalescence. These results provide the baseline and predictions needed for future jet-tagged charmed-hadron measurements in both collision systems.
papers.summary: This study measures the Λc+/D0 ratio inside jets in pp and Pb+Pb collisions to distinguish between color reconnection and coalescence hadronization mechanisms. It finds that color reconnection enhances the ratio at low pT in jets while coalescence suppresses it, providing a jet-based discriminator for non-fragmentation hadronization.

papers.title: $N \to \Delta$ Transition Form Factors in the Thermal AdS/QCD Soft-Wall Model with Modified Propagators
papers.authors: Narmin Nasibova, Xerxes D. Arsiwalla, Shakir Nagiyev
papers.abstract: We investigate electromagnetic (EM) and axial vector (AV) form factors of the nucleon-Delta baryon transition within the thermal AdS/QCD soft-wall model. While the vector bulk-to-boundary propagator admits a well-behaved analytical solution, the transverse axial vector equation of motion involves the vacuum expectation value of the bifundamental scalar (generating chiral symmetry breaking). Due to this, the axial propagator diverges asymptotically, rendering it unsuitable for computing observables in the soft-wall model. To address this problem, we implement a regularization for the axial propagator in the form of a momentum-dependent cut-off, that identifies its correct physical regime. This is achieved via an interior constraint approach to the boundary-value problem, that determines the cut-off point. The consistency of this procedure is verified near the UV limit. As a proof of concept, we test this modified propagator (and also a parametrically deformed version of it) to estimate axial vector form factors of the $N \to \Delta$ transition, and find results moderately comparable with form factor profiles from experimental observations, lattice QCD, and other theoretical models. Equipped with this regularization, the thermal soft-wall model becomes a useful tool to probe thermal characteristics of QCD form factors. We demonstrate this for both, the EM and AV sectors of the $N \to \Delta$ transition.
papers.summary: The paper develops a thermal AdS/QCD soft‑wall model to compute electromagnetic and axial‑vector form factors for the (N	oDelta) transition, introducing a momentum‑dependent regulator for the divergent axial propagator. The resulting form factors show reasonable agreement with experiment, lattice data, and other models, demonstrating the model’s utility for probing thermal QCD observables.

papers.title: Perturbations and phenomenology of compact objects in quantum gravity theories
papers.authors: Andrea Spina
papers.abstract: This thesis investigates the perturbative dynamics and phenomenology of compact objects in two approaches to quantum gravity: quadratic gravity and asymptotic safety. Linear perturbations provide a tool to probe the physical properties of spacetimes and their potential observational signatures, including quasinormal modes, black hole shadows, and Hawking radiation. The first part focuses on Einstein-Weyl gravity, where an additional massive spin-2 degree of freedom modifies the dynamics of compact objects. We derive and analyze tensor perturbation for static, spherically symmetric solutions, identifying Gregory-Laflamme-type instabilities in the monopole sector and studying the time domain evolution of higher multipoles. We also investigate universal massive-field tails and the breakdown of the standard eikonal correspondence between quasinormal modes and null geodesics. Particular attention is devoted to veiled singularities, horizonless configurations that satisfy a form of weak cosmic censorship and can mimic black hole shadows. The second part examines regular black holes in asymptotically safe gravity. Using the proper-time flow approach, we construct and investigate a dynamical regular black hole solution arising from gravitational collapse. We analyze its perturbative stability and quasinormal mode spectrum, finding characteristic deviations from Schwarzschild black holes. We explore the phenomenological implications of quantum corrections for shadows and Hawking radiation. While shadow remains compatible with current constraints, the modified evaporation process features lower temperatures and suppressed emission rates, with implications for primordial black holes and their possible contribution to dark matter. Overall, this work demonstrates how the perturbative dynamics of compact objects can connect quantum gravity models to potentially observable astrophysical phenomena.
papers.summary: This thesis studies linear perturbations of compact objects in quadratic gravity and asymptotically safe gravity, deriving quasinormal modes, shadow properties, and Hawking radiation signatures. It identifies instabilities in Einstein-Weyl gravity, constructs regular black holes from collapse, and discusses phenomenological implications for primordial black holes and dark matter.

papers.title: ${\mathcal{O}}(\alpha_s^2\alpha)$ threshold corrections to inclusive $Z$-boson production
papers.authors: Tanmoy Pati, Narayan Rana, Avick Saha
papers.abstract: To match the experimental precision targeted by future collider programs, theoretical predictions for Drell-Yan production must incorporate higher-order mixed Quantum Chromodynamics and electroweak corrections. In this work, we present for the first time the ${\mathcal{O}}(\alpha_s^2\alpha)$ corrections to the inclusive cross-section for $Z$-boson production in the threshold limit. By systematically evaluating the missing singlet contributions, we obtain the complete set of ${\mathcal{O}}(\alpha_s^2\alpha)$ quark form factors, which we use to construct the soft-virtual cross-section by exploiting renormalization group invariance, the K+G evolution equation, and universal soft-collinear factorization. Our results capture the dominant threshold logarithmic enhancements, improve the theoretical scale uncertainties, significantly reduce electroweak input scheme dependence, and establish a crucial step toward complete ${\mathcal{O}}(\alpha_s^2\alpha)$ corrections indispensable for future precision programs.
papers.summary: This paper computes the missing ${mathcal{O}}(alpha_s^2alpha)$ corrections to the inclusive Z‑boson production cross‑section in the threshold limit, providing the complete set of quark form factors and a soft‑virtual cross‑section via RG invariance and the K+G equation. The improved predictions reduce scale uncertainties and electroweak scheme dependence, offering a critical step toward precision phenomenology.

papers.title: Plabic promotions beyond cluster: quantum cluster structures and the dual canonical basis
papers.authors: Jian-Rong Li, Michael Oren Perlstein, Ran J. Tessler
papers.abstract: Plabic tangles define geometric promotion maps between configurations and, after choosing a lift, between Grassmannians. The main conjecture in \cite{Tangles} is that when the tangle is dominant and solvable the induced algebraic promotion is cluster quasi-homomorphism. This work extends the cluster perspective in two directions. First, we initiate the study of quantum promotions. We conjecture that all promotions defined from dominant solvable tangles are naturally lifted to a \emph{quantum cluster quasi homomorphism}, and prove for all cases in the literature that the were shown to be (classical) cluster quasi-homomorphisms. Secondly, we define the notion of cluster-Lusztig quasi-homomorphisms, which are cluster quasi homomorphisms that take Lustig's dual canonical basis elements to dual canonical basis element, up to a Laurent monomial in frozen variables, with clearing and normalization chosen uniformly on each content component. We prove the unexpected result that the classical and quantum $m$-unary star promotions fall into this category, and conjecture that all promotions coming from dominant solvable tangles share the same property. We then consider promotions via non solvable cores of intersection number higher than one. We use it to study facets of amplituhedron cells, and to show that some of them do not lie in zero loci of dual canonical basis elements, disproving a conjecture by T. Lam \cite{LamGP}.
papers.summary: This paper extends the theory of plabic tangles, proving that dominant solvable tangles give rise to quantum cluster quasi‑homomorphisms that preserve dual canonical basis elements, and applies these results to study facets of amplituhedron cells, finding counterexamples to a conjecture about dual canonical basis vanishing loci. The work links combinatorial cluster structures with geometric objects relevant to scattering amplitudes, offering new tools for analyzing higher‑point amplitude configurations.
